belief: People are always staring and judging me.
origins: Self-consciousness can make us feel watched, especially after trauma, bullying, or visible differences. Often others are absorbed in their own concerns, but the feeling of being watched is vivid.
teaches: “O LORD, You have searched me and known me.” Psalm 139 shows that we are always seen by God, and seen with love. “The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.” People notice less than we fear, and when they do stare, it often reflects curiosity or their own discomfort. God’s view of you is kind: “He will quiet you with His love.”
self_statements: I cannot go anywhere without being stared at.
errors: Believing people either ignore me or judge me.
Feeling exposed and concluding that I am being judged.
Calling myself the center of attention.
questions: How often do I truly notice others’ appearance?
What evidence do I have that people are judging?
What do I do to avoid being seen, and what does it cost?
What does God see when He looks at me?
What would a small experiment look like, such as going out for ten minutes?
truth: People notice me less than I fear, and God’s gaze on me is loving. I can step out in small steps, with trusted company, and let His acceptance steady me.
hw_truths: The fear of man is a snare.
The Lord knows and loves me.
He quiets me with His love.
Most people are focused on themselves.
log: Each week, note one outing and what actually happened.
actions: Count actual stares during an outing.
prayer: Lord, I feel watched. Quiet me with Your love, and give me courage to live among people without fear. Amen.
